arxiv-1412-0749.title: Quantum spin Hall states in graphene interacting with WS 2 or WSe 2
arxiv-1412-0749.creator: T. P. Kaloni 1, L. Kou 2, T. Frauenheim 2, U. Schwingenschlögl 1,
arxiv-1412-0749.description: A 2014 arXiv research paper by T. P. Kaloni 1, L. Kou 2, T. Frauenheim 2, U. Schwingenschlögl 1,. In the framework of first-principles calculations, we investigate the structural and electronic properties of graphene in contact with as well as sandwiched between WS 2 and WSe 2 monolayers. We report the modification of the band characteristics due to the interaction at the interface and demonstrate that the presence of the dichalcogenides results in quantum spin Hall states in the absence of a magnetic field.

arxiv-2103-13275.title: When Word Embeddings Become Endangered
arxiv-2103-13275.creator: Khalid Alnajjar
arxiv-2103-13275.description: Abstract Big languages such as English and Finnish have many natural language processing (NLP) resources and models, but this is not the case for low-resourced and endangered languages as such resources are so scarce despite the great advantages they would provide for the language communities.

arxiv-2103-16324.title: Automated Cleanup of the ImageNet Dataset by Model Consensus, Explainability and Confident Learning
arxiv-2103-16324.creator: Csaba Kertész
arxiv-2103-16324.description: Abstract The convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on ILSVRC12 ImageNet were the backbone of various applications as a generic classifier, a feature extractor or a base model for transfer learning. This paper describes automated heuristics based on model consensus, explainability and confident learning to correct labeling mistakes and remove ambiguous images from this dataset.

arxiv-2110-01005.title: Cerberus : Query-driven Scalable Vulnerability Detection in OAuth Service Provider Implementations Conference: Proceedings of the 2022 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security; November 7–11, 2022; Los Angeles, CA, USA Proceedings of the 2022 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer an
arxiv-2110-01005.creator: Tamjid Al Rahat, Yu Feng, Yuan Tian
arxiv-2110-01005.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Tamjid Al Rahat, Yu Feng, Yuan Tian. OAuth protocols have been widely adopted to simplify user authentication and service authorization for third-party applications. However, little effort has been devoted to automatically checking the security of the libraries that service providers widely use. In this paper, we formalize the OAuth specifications and security best practices, and design Cerberus , an automated static analyzer, to find logical flaws and identify vulnerabilities in the implementation of OAuth service provider libraries.

arxiv-2110-09306.title: Two-stage Fourth-order Gas Kinetic Solver-based Compact Subcell Finite Volume Method for Compressible Flows over Triangular Meshes
arxiv-2110-09306.creator: Chao Zhang, Qibing Li, Peng Song, Jiequan Li
arxiv-2110-09306.description: Abstract To meet the demand for complex geometries and high resolutions of small-scale flow structures, a two-stage fourth-order subcell finite volume (SCFV) method combining the gas-kinetic solver (GKS) with subcell techniques for compressible flows over (unstructured) triangular meshes was developed to improve the compactness and efficiency.

arxiv-2304-08898.title: Galaxy pairs in The Three Hundred simulations II: studying bound ones and identifying them via machine learning 2021 Galaxy pairs in The Three Hundred simulations II: studying bound ones and identifying them via machine learning – B
arxiv-2304-08898.creator: Ana Contreras-Santos, Alexander Knebe, Weiguang Cui, Roan Haggar, Frazer Pearce, Meghan Gray, Marco De Petris, Gustavo Yepes
arxiv-2304-08898.description: Abstract Using the data set of The Three Hundred project, i.e. 324 hydrodynamical resimulations of cluster-sized haloes and the regions of radius 15 h − 1 ​ Mpc {{h^{-1}{\rm Mpc}}} around them, we study galaxy pairs in high-density environments. By projecting the galaxies’ 3D coordinates onto a 2D plane, we apply observational techniques to find galaxy pairs.

arxiv-2401-06920.title: Comparing GPT-4 and Open-Source Language Models in Misinformation Mitigation
arxiv-2401-06920.creator: Tyler Vergho, Jean-François Godbout, Reihaneh Rabbany, Kellin Pelrine
arxiv-2401-06920.description: Abstract Recent large language models (LLMs) have been shown to be effective for misinformation detection. However, the choice of LLMs for experiments varies widely, leading to uncertain conclusions. In particular, GPT-4 is known to be strong in this domain, but it is closed source, potentially expensive, and can show instability between different versions. Meanwhile, alternative LLMs have given mixed results.

arxiv-2409-01477.title: Compatible Gradient Approximations for Actor-Critic Algorithms
arxiv-2409-01477.creator: Baturay Saglam and Dionysis Kalogerias Department of ECE—Yale University { baturay.saglam , dionysis.kalogerias }@yale.edu
arxiv-2409-01477.description: Abstract Deterministic policy gradient algorithms are foundational for actor-critic methods in controlling continuous systems, yet they often encounter inaccuracies due to their dependence on the derivative of the critic’s value estimates with respect to input actions. This reliance requires precise action-value gradient computations, a task that proves challenging under function approximation.

pmc-10643623.title: Dehazing in hyperspectral images: the GRANHHADA database
pmc-10643623.creator: Sol Fernández Carvelo, Miguel Ángel Martínez Domingo, Eva M. Valero, Javier Hernández Andrés
pmc-10643623.description: In this study, we present an analysis of dehazing techniques for hyperspectral images in outdoor scenes. The aim of our research is to compare different dehazing approaches for hyperspectral images and introduce a new hyperspectral image database called GRANHHADA (GRANada Hyperspectral HAzy Database) containing 35 scenes with various haze conditions.

pmc-11295351.title: Heat-killed probiotic Levilactobacillus brevis MKAK9 and its exopolysaccharide promote longevity by modulating aging hallmarks and enhancing immune responses in Caenorhabditis elegans
pmc-11295351.creator: Arun Kumar, Manti Kumar Saha, Vipin Kumar, Anupam Bhattacharya, Sagar Barge, Ashis K. Mukherjee, Mohan C. Kalita, Mojibur R. Khan
pmc-11295351.description: BackgroundProteostasis is a critical aging hallmark responsible for removing damaged or misfolded proteins and their aggregates by improving proteasomal degradation through the autophagy-lysosome pathway (ALP) and the ubiquitin–proteasome system (UPS). Research on the impact of heat-killed probiotic bacteria and their structural components on aging hallmarks and innate immune responses is scarce, yet enhancing these effects could potentially delay age-related diseases.

pmc-12496562.title: A New Minimally Invasive Technique for Anterior Resin‐Bonded Fixed Dental Prostheses: A 5‐Year Clinical Report
pmc-12496562.creator: Abdulaziz Samran
pmc-12496562.description: This clinical report describes the use of a new design for resin‐bonded fixed dental prostheses (RBFDP) to replace a missing maxillary right central incisor. This report illustrates a conservative, functional, and esthetic RBFDP made of a metal‐ceramic framework. Using RBFDP allowed for achieving acceptable esthetics with a conservative and functional result.

pmc-13079573.title: Asking for help: the development of a simulation-based mental health application to enhance depression literacy, mental health communication, and help-seeking among Black autistic youth
pmc-13079573.creator: Ed-Dee G. Williams, Fatima Vakil, Oluwatobi Abubakare, Angelina Latin, Lauren Ware, David Nelson, Matthew J. Smith
pmc-13079573.description: Black autistic youth experience disproportionately high rates of depression and face intersecting barriers such as racial discrimination, stigma, and limited access to care, yet few interventions address their needs. This study introduces Asking for Help (A4H), a culturally responsive, simulation-based intervention designed to improve depression literacy and help-seeking skills through an e-learning module and interactive conversation practice.

pmc-13232440.creator: Jaron X. Y. Tan, Pan Liu
pmc-13232440.description: In Canada, about 1.7 million individuals experience an eating disorder at any given time. Early adolescence is a high-risk period for the onset of disordered eating attitudes and behaviors; without timely intervention, these problems may persist into adulthood and predict a host of negative outcomes.
